About the Practice

Staten Island University Hospital, part of Northwell Health, is a 668-bed specialized teaching hospital and a major tertiary referral center in Staten Island, New York City. [2, 5] It provides world-class health care with a wide range of specialty programs and advanced medical care across its two campuses and numerous community-based centers. [1, 5] Key areas of expertise and specialized units include cardiology and cardiothoracic surgery (recognized among America's Best Hospitals for Cardiac Surgery and Coronary Intervention), cancer care (Florina Cancer Center, Comprehensive Breast Cancer Center), burn care (Regional Burn Center), bariatric surgery, sleep medicine, Level III Perinatal Center, stroke care (Stroke Center, Primary Stroke Center, Comprehensive Stroke Center), comprehensive inpatient rehabilitation, geriatric psychiatry, behavioral health care, and substance abuse services. [1, 2, 5, 8] It is also a Level I Adult Trauma Center and Level II Pediatric Trauma Center. [2] The hospital is recognized for high performance in various specialties including geriatrics, neurology and neurosurgery, orthopedics, and pulmonology and lung surgery, and is a significant teaching hospital affiliated with universities like SUNY Downstate and Touro College. [1, 2]

Electronic Health Record System

FollowMyHealth

Primary Electronic Health Record System

Research Analysis
Methodology & Findings

Staten Island University Hospital (SIUH), a member of Northwell Health, utilizes the FollowMyHealth patient portal for patient access to their health information. This portal is a product of Veradigm, formerly Allscripts. Northwell Health has historically used Allscripts' EHR systems, specifically Allscripts Sunrise in its hospitals and Allscripts TouchWorks in its outpatient practices. However, Northwell Health announced in March 2023 a strategic agreement with Epic to implement Epic's integrated electronic health record system across its entire health system. This transition to Epic is being rolled out in phases, with the first phase beginning in 2025. Therefore, while SIUH currently uses the FollowMyHealth patient portal connected to their existing EHR system, Northwell Health is in the process of transitioning to the Epic EHR system, which typically uses the MyChart patient portal. This indicates that a change in the patient portal is likely as the Epic implementation progresses across the Northwell Health system.
